title: 01 · Primitives & dimensions
equation: T[i,j], L[i], d[n,i,j], theta[j], alpha[n,j], gamma[j]
explanation: Explicit industry axes; positive primitives and preference shares. Demand-share rows sum to one without renormalization. Domestic costs are one in every industry.

title: 02 · Delivered unit costs
explanation: Labor moves between domestic industries, so one exporter wage applies to every industry. Labor does not move internationally.

title: 03 · Trade shares
explanation: Sum over exporter axis 1, independently within each importer and industry. The (N,J) log denominator broadcasts back across exporters.

title: 04 · Industry prices
explanation: Each industry's elasticity and fixed gamma determine its price index. Gamma is unchanged by the counterfactual.

title: 05 · Aggregate cost of living
explanation: Normalized Cobb–Douglas utility gives a weighted geometric mean of industry prices. There are no additional preference constants in C. Real wages are w/C. For J=1, alpha=1 returns the sole industry price exactly.

title: 06 · Market clearing
equation: X[n,j] = alpha[n,j] income[n]; sales[i] = sum_n sum_j pi[n,i,j]X[n,j]
explanation: Aggregate importer spending over all industries to determine each exporter's sales. Balanced trade applies to country totals, not separately to each industry.

title: 07 · Levels entry point
equation: unit wages → fixed-damping wage iteration → final economic objects
explanation: The levels route supplies its own shares, prices and incomes. The shared wage loop starts at unit wages and retains the final evaluated state.

title: 08 · Explicit iteration loop
equation: evaluate → full residual check → simultaneous wage update → normalize → repeat
explanation: Every evaluated state is recorded. The loop stops only when the full residual is below the target, the update limit is reached, or the numerical state is invalid. Defaults: damping 0.2, target 1e-13, maximum 10,000 updates.

title: 09 · Damping & normalization
explanation: Fixed damping 0.2 is a numerical control distinct from demand shares alpha[n,j]. Update wages simultaneously, then normalize country 0.

title: 01 · Baseline statistics & shock
explanation: A converged baseline supplies shares and country incomes. Preferences and elasticities stay fixed. Shocked cost levels must remain admissible in every industry.

title: 02 · Counterfactual shares
explanation: Reweight each industry's baseline shares. This route never calls levels competitiveness or reads counterfactual levels wages.

title: 03 · Industry price changes
explanation: The exponent applies to each importer/industry exporter sum. Fixed industry gamma cancels from price ratios.

title: 04 · Aggregate price changes
explanation: Fixed preferences imply that the ratio of aggregate levels indices is this product of industry price hats. Demand and market clearing are unchanged by utility normalization.

title: 05 · Country spending
equation: income1[n] = income0[n] w_hat[n]; X1[n,j] = alpha[n,j] income1[n]
explanation: Fixed labor makes wage hats scale country incomes. Allocate spending using fixed alpha before summing exporter sales over importers and industries.

title: 06 · Hat equilibrium solver
explanation: The shared wage loop uses independently calculated hat economics. Welfare changes use aggregate cost-of-living hats.

title: 07 · Full convergence check
equation: finite positive state AND max_i |r[i]| < 1e-13 → converged
explanation: Every country participates in the residual check, including country 0. Small wage changes alone are not a stopping rule. Limits and invalid numerical states return explicit failure statuses.

title: 01 · Fix the experiment
explanation: Three countries, two heterogeneous industries; only industry 0's two bilateral costs fall. Industry 1's equilibrium still responds through wages.

title: 02 · Solve E0 and E1
equation: E0 = levels(primitives); E1 = levels(primitives with d1=d0*d_hat)
explanation: Both solves start at unit wages. Technologies, labor, elasticities, preferences and gamma stay fixed.

title: 03 · Solve hats from E0
explanation: The same shock reaches the independent route through E0's expenditure shares and incomes.

title: 04 · Compare normalized changes
equation: w1/w0, P1/P0, C1/C0, pi1/pi0, real_wage1/real_wage0 versus hats
explanation: Five comparisons cover 3 wages, 6 industry prices, 3 aggregate prices, 18 bilateral industry share ratios, and 3 welfare changes. All three routes must converge.

title: 05 · Apply both strict bounds
explanation: The denominator is the levels-route ratio, not the change minus one. The two error tests are separate, so one cannot compensate for the other.

title: 06 · Record evidence
equation: PASS = converged(E0,E1,hats) AND every comparison passes
explanation: The builder runs this exact verification routine, embeds its certificate, and hashes the reviewed source. A completed run is not itself a pass.

title: 07 · J=1 regression
equation: J=1, alpha[:,0]=1 → accepted one-industry E0, E1 and exact hats
explanation: Compare 18 objects against immutable data captured before code changes at the accepted PR #4 revision. Separate absolute and relative bounds and convergence apply. There is no duplicate historical solver.
